Uncertainty: differences inside the strong-H-bond block are small (<1 kcal/mol) since all have nearly identical 7-membered H-bond rings; the relative placement of the weakly interacting folded forms (26, 21, 24) versus the fully extended non-bonded forms (9, 29, 2) is the least certain part of the ranking.

STRUCTURE: All 30 files are the same molecule, a cyclopropane bearing OH on C7 (the quaternary ring carbon, atom 15 = O) and OH on the adjacent ring CH (atom 10 = O), with a CH2-C(=O)-CH3 (acetonyl) arm on C7. Ring C-C distances are all ~1.50 A (intact cyclopropane, no differential ring strain). Checking the ring-plane normal against the C7->O15 and C9->O10 vectors shows the two oxygens lie on OPPOSITE faces in every conformer (O10...O15 = 3.6-3.7 A): the diol is trans, so no direct intramolecular OH...OH bond is geometrically possible in any conformer. Consequently the only strong stabilization available is an OH donating to the ketone oxygen O3, and there are two possible motifs: (A) O15-H...O3, a 6-membered pseudo-ring (O15-C7-C4-C2=O3), and (B) O10-H...O3, a 7-membered pseudo-ring that exploits the rigid C9-C7 ring bond.

H-BOND SURVEY (H...O distance / O-H...O angle):
B-type (near-linear, strongest): 26 (1.87 A, 159 deg), 15 (1.88, 157), 5 (1.91, 157), 28 (1.95, 150), 13 (1.96, 149), 21 (2.02, 141).
A-type (short but bent, because the donor sits on the substituted ring carbon): 1 (1.97, 138), 29 (2.05, 132), 3 (2.06, 130), 11 (2.07, 131), 6 (2.14, 128).
Weak/marginal: 8 (bifurcated, both OH toward O3: 2.48/117 and 2.63/121), 22 (2.33/124), 12 (2.34/126), 24 (2.50/127), 20 (2.46/112, badly bent), 4 (2.78), 17 (2.80), 18 (2.91), 9 (3.05).
No H-bond at all (both OH point into free space, all O...O >3.5 A): 2, 7, 10, 14, 16, 19, 23, 25, 27, 30.

SECOND FACTOR - KETONE TORSION O3=C2-C4-C7 (propanal/butanone-like profile: minimum near 0 deg, ~1-2 kcal penalty near 60-90 deg, second shallow minimum near 130 deg): computed values: 26 = 56, 15 = 58, 5 = 72, 13 = 74, 28 = 80, 1 = 58, 21 = 50, 29 = 24, 3 = 22, 11 = 29, 6 = 14. So the B-type (7-ring) conformers pay a modest eclipsing/barrier-region penalty for folding the arm, whereas the A-type (6-ring) conformers happen to keep the near-ideal syn arrangement. This partly compensates the weaker, bent A-type H-bond, which is the main source of uncertainty in the middle of the ranking.

OTHER CHECKS: no O...O contacts below ~2.75 A other than the H-bonded pairs (so no lone-pair/lone-pair repulsion anywhere); no H...H contacts below ~2.1 A in the H-bonded conformers; the free OH in every top conformer points into open space (no clash with the methyl or the ring CH2). Among the non-bonded conformers the only remaining discriminators are the ketone torsion and dipole orientation: 2, 30, 19, 10, 7, 9 keep the C=O roughly anti/skew to the C-O dipoles (torsion 120-145 deg, second minimum), while 14, 23, 25, 27, 16 sit near the eclipsing barrier region (80-90 deg) with the two C-O dipoles roughly parallel, which is the worst combination.

RANKING LOGIC: (i) short, near-linear O10-H...O3 seven-membered H-bond wins (26, 15, 5, 28, 13); (ii) then conformers trading a slightly bent H-bond for a better ketone torsion (29, 1, 21, 3, 11, 6); (iii) then the weak/bifurcated contacts (8, 24, 22, 12, 4, 17); (iv) then non-H-bonded conformers ordered by ketone torsion and dipole opposition, with the eclipsed, dipole-aligned ones last (16, 27, 25, 23, 14). Differences within tiers (especially 5/13/28 vs 29/1, and the whole non-bonded block) are only a few tenths of a kcal/mol and are the least certain part of this ordering.

All 30 files are the same molecule, CH3-CH(OH)-CH(CHO)-C(=O)CH3 (3-(1-hydroxyethyl)... i.e. an aldehyde and a methyl ketone on the same central CH, with a secondary alcohol on the adjacent carbon). I measured H(hydroxyl)...O distances/angles and the C=O/C=O vector angle for each structure.

6 (152 deg, essentially anti carbonyls, no close contacts), 17 (147 deg), 14 (144 deg), 25 (142 deg), 12 (141 deg), 7 (132 deg), 9 (127 deg), 11 (122 deg), 4 (114 deg), 2 (113 deg), 16 (109 deg), 30 (108 deg), 23 (108 deg), 5 (102 deg), 22 (95 deg). All 30 structures are the same 2-ethyl-5-(hydroxymethyl)-1H-pyrrole, so the ring is unstrained and identical everywhere; the only energy differences come from three rotors: (i) N10-C9-C12-O15 (orientation of the CH2OH), (ii) C9-C12-O15-H16 (OH), and (iii) N10-C6-C5-C1 (ethyl). I classified each conformer by internal distances that are independent of the arbitrary frame.

CH2OH rotamer (from d(O...N10) and d(O...C8), calibrated on model geometry: syn-N ~2.7/3.7, perpendicular ~3.3/3.3, syn-C8 ~3.7/3.0):
- phi ~ 0 (O eclipsing N, in plane): 24 (2.70/3.69) and 27 (2.70/3.69). These two are the only ones with a genuine N-H...O contact: d(H11...O)=2.38 (24) and 2.41 (27). The N-H...O angle is only ~96 deg (a 5-membered arrangement), so it is not a textbook H-bond, but the acidic pyrrole N-H sits 2.4 A from the alcohol oxygen, an electrostatically favourable, dipole-cancelling contact. Both also have the OH anti (d(H16...C9)=3.21, i.e. C9-C12-O-H ~180, the intrinsically preferred staggered O-H) and a perpendicular ethyl, so they carry no compensating penalty and are placed first.
- phi ~ 65 (O slightly rotated toward the NH side, out of plane): 11, 5, 29, 21, 4, 10, 12 (3.02-3.05/3.53). Here d(O...H11) ~3.0, a long-range favourable electrostatic contact, plus the C-O bond is out of plane (good sigma*C-O/pi hyperconjugation).
- phi ~ 100 (essentially perpendicular): 25, 16, 23, 3, 8, 2, 17, 30, 18 (3.34-3.39/3.26-3.30). Also unstrained, but the O is now 3.6 A from the N-H, so it loses the weak electrostatic bonus.
- phi ~ 130: 7, 15, 1, 6 (3.47-3.53/3.12-3.19). Partly rotated toward the C8-H side; slightly less hyperconjugative stabilisation.
- phi ~ 180 (O in plane, eclipsing C8): 28, 26, 9, 20, 13, 14, 22, 19 (3.68/2.97). The C-O bond lies in the ring plane (loss of the benzylic perpendicular preference) and the OH hydrogen is pushed against the C4-H: d(H16...H17)=2.33-2.34 in 26 and 20, 2.56-2.59 in 22, 19, 28, 9, 13, 14. Only a weak C-H...O (O...H17 ~2.87) compensates, so this family is ranked lowest apart from the clashing conformer 12.

OH rotamer: in 28 of 30 structures d(H16...C9)=2.49-2.58, i.e. the O-H is gauche; only 24 and 27 have it anti (3.21). No conformer places the hydroxyl H over the ring pi face (H16...ring-centroid is 3.3-3.4 A everywhere with O-H...C angles of only ~75 deg), so no OH...pi stabilisation differentiates them.

Ethyl rotamer (from d(C1...N) and d(C1...C7)): perpendicular (C1...N = 3.20-3.23) in 11, 25, 16, 23, 26, 5, 8, 7, 20, 15, 17, 29, 30, 24, 27, 22, 6, 19; in-plane with CH3 eclipsing C7 (C1...N = 3.72-3.79, C1...C7 ~3.0, one CH3-H...H18 contact of 2.5-2.6) in 28, 21, 3, 9, 13, 2, 4, 10, 14, 18, 1. Because the exocyclic angles of a five-membered aromatic are wide (~126 deg) the in-plane form is only mildly worse; I apply a small penalty. Conformer 12 is unique: the methyl is eclipsing the N side (C1...N = 2.87, C1...H11 = 2.60, CH3-H...H(N) = 2.41). This is a real steric clash against the N-H and makes 12 clearly the least stable.

No other short nonbonded contacts (<2.3 A) or distorted rings occur, so most gaps are small (a few tenths of a kcal/mol) and the ordering inside each rotamer family (settled by minor differences in H16...H11, H16...H17 and CH3...H contacts) is genuinely uncertain. The confident statements are: 24/27 best (N-H...O contact plus anti-OH and perpendicular ethyl); the in-plane-O family (28, 26, 9, 20, 13, 14, 22, 19) low; 12 worst.

The molecule is 3-hydroxy-3-methylhex-5-ynal: a quaternary-like carbinol carbon C5 bearing CH3, OH (O6-H7), a CH2-CHO arm (C8-C9(=O10)H11) and a propargyl arm (C14-C15≡C16-H17). All conformers are strain-free acyclic chains, so the dominant energy differences come from (i) the intramolecular O-H···O=C hydrogen bond, which closes a favourable six-membered ring (H7-O6-C5-C8-C9=O10), (ii) a weaker O-H···π(C≡C) interaction (five-membered pseudo-ring, geometrically limited to ~120-125 deg), (iii) very weak aldehyde C-H···O(H) contacts, and (iv) absence of any of these (dipoles unpaired). Measured H7···O10 distances/O-H···O angles: 30 (1.94 A, 142 deg) is clearly the best hydrogen bond; then 28 (2.07 A, 133 deg), 17 (2.08 A, 132 deg), 20 (2.11 A, 130 deg), 23 (2.12 A, 128 deg), 10 (2.14 A, 128 deg). In 28 the hydroxyl O also sits only 2.90 A from alkyne C15, a mildly crowded contact, so it is placed just below 17. A second family has the OH turned onto the triple bond: H7···C15 / H7···(C15C16 midpoint) = 8 (2.38/2.55), 11 (2.43/2.60), 7 (2.43/2.60), 29 (2.44/2.60), 9 (2.46/2.63), 2 (2.47/2.65), 3 (2.47/2.65), 6 (2.47/2.65), 27 (2.48/2.65), 25 (2.48/2.65), 15 (2.51/2.71), 21 (2.52/2.71), 19 (2.59/2.51). These OH···π contacts are worth appreciably less than the O-H···O=C bond, so the whole family ranks below the six hydrogen-bonded structures; within it, 8, 25 and 7 gain a little extra from a simultaneous aldehyde C-H···O6 contact (2.5-2.7 A), while 21 and 15 have the longest, most bent OH···π geometry. The remaining eleven conformers (22, 5, 14, 13, 18, 1, 26, 16, 12, 4, 24) have the hydroxyl proton pointing into empty space: H7···O10 is 3.3-5 A and H7···alkyne is 3.4-5 A with the O-H vector directed away from the pi cloud (negative projection), so no donor is used. Among these, 22 and 5 retain a weak aldehyde C-H···O6 contact (~2.47-2.48 A) plus a long (3.46-3.47 A) OH/alkyne approach, 14 has a 3.48 A OH/alkyne approach, 13 has a long 3.33 A O-H···O=C alignment, and 18, 1, 26, 16 keep only a weak C-H···O contact (2.48-2.73 A). Conformers 12, 4 and 24 show no compensating contact at all, with both polar groups splayed apart (H7 more than 4.9 A from both the carbonyl O and the alkyne), making them the least stabilized. Uncertainty: the internal ordering inside the hydrogen-bonded set (differences of only 0.05-0.2 A in H···O) and inside the large OH···π set is small (probably well under 1 kcal/mol), and the relative weight of an OH···π contact versus a bent, long O-H···O contact (conformer 13) is the least certain judgement here.

All 30 files are the same molecule: cis-2-(2-hydroxyethyl)-3-methyltetrahydrofuran (ring C2-C3-C4-O9-C10; methyl on C2, -CH2CH2OH on C10). Chirality tests (signed volumes at C2 and C10) give the same signs in every structure, so all are conformers of one diastereomer (methyl and side chain cis on the ring). Therefore the energy differences must come from (i) the intramolecular O-H(hydroxyl)...O(ring ether) hydrogen bond, which closes a six-membered ring (O9-C10-C11-C13-O15-H16), (ii) the two rotatable chain torsions O9-C10-C11-C13 and C10-C11-C13-O15 (gauche vs anti, eclipsing), and (iii) ring pucker/steric contacts (which are nearly constant: the cis 1,2-relationship fixes C1...C11 at ~2.9-3.0 A in every structure).

H-bond survey (H16...O9 / O15...O9 / O-H...O angle): 3 (1.98/2.78/139), 12 (1.98/2.79/139), 5 (1.98/2.78/139), 23 (2.00/2.81/140), 17 (2.01/2.77/134), 14 (2.10/2.80/128). All other conformers have H16...O9 > 3.2 A (27: 2.58 A but with a poor 119 deg angle, 2: 3.20 A) and thus no real H bond. Six-membered intramolecular OH...O(ether) bonding is worth ~3 kcal/mol, so these six structures head the list.

Within the H-bonded set the chain torsions decide the order. Computed torsions O9-C10-C11-C13 / C10-C11-C13-O15: 5 = 58/70, 12 = 60/71, 23 = 65/71, 3 = 48/74, 17 = 29/75, 14 = 26/52. 5 and 12 are essentially ideal gauche-gauche with an almost linear H bond; 23 is nearly as good; 3 pays some eclipsing at both torsions; 17 and especially 14 have the O9-C10-C11-C13 torsion driven to ~25-30 deg (O9...C13 only 2.78 and 2.70 A), i.e. strongly eclipsed, which also bends the H bond (134 and 128 deg). Hence 5 ~ 12 > 23 > 3 > 17 > 14.

For the non-bonded (no-HB) conformers I scored the two chain torsions with a threefold term plus a gauche penalty, and checked O...O separations and short contacts. Fully extended anti/anti chains are best: 30 (162/180) and 8 (153/180) have no gauche interactions and no close contacts. Next come single-gauche/anti conformers with near-ideal angles: 29 (57/180), 15 (55/180), 19 (50/180), 18 (48/180), 9 (47/180), 7 (47/180), then 6 (162/56), 1 (167/73), 10 (158/62). Conformers with two gauche torsions but no H bond suffer both torsional and O/O dipole cost and are worse: 2 (51/60, weak 3.2 A OH...O), 27 (37/50, only a bent 2.58 A contact), 4, 28, 21, 20, 26 (all ~55-65/55-65 with O...O ~3.7 A). Clearly strained ones have torsions near the 90-135 deg eclipsing region: 25 (162/79), 13 (149/54), 24 (49/93), 11 (149/78), 16 (131/64), 22 (135/74); 16 and 22 are the worst, with the O-C-C-C torsion sitting almost exactly on the rotational maximum.

Uncertainties: the top four (5, 12, 23, 3) differ by only a few tenths of a kcal/mol and their order could easily permute; the placement of 14 and 17 (H-bonded but eclipsed) relative to the best extended non-H-bonded conformers (30, 29, 15) is the largest single uncertainty, since it trades ~3 kcal of H bonding against ~2 kcal of torsional strain. Ring-pucker differences (all rings are normally puckered, no near-planar rings) were treated as a minor, roughly constant contribution.

Connectivity (identical in all files) is CH3–CH(CHO)–CH2–O–CH=NH: a 2-methyl-3-(formimidoyloxy)propanal-type chain with an aldehyde, an ether O and an imine N–H. Rotatable degrees of freedom that matter: (i) the formimidate O–CH=NH unit, (ii) tau2 = C5–C9–O12–C13 (rotation about CH2–O), (iii) tau1 = C6–C5–C9–O12 (backbone), (iv) the aldehyde rotamer about C5–C6, plus any close nonbonded contacts.

1) Formimidate unit: in every structure d(C9...N14) = 2.60-2.70 A while d(C9...H16) is >3.2 A, i.e. the alkyl group is syn to the C=N (the ester-like 'Z' arrangement) and d(O12...H15) is ~3.15 A everywhere (N–H anti to O). So all 30 share the low-energy planar formimidate geometry; this is NOT a discriminator.

2) A striking discriminator: four conformers (12, 20, 29, 30) show an extremely short imine-N...aldehyde-C contact, d(N14...C6) = 2.10-2.13 A (with O7...N14 only 2.64-2.69 A), i.e. the N lone pair sits almost bonded on top of the carbonyl carbon closing a 6-membered ring; the carbonyl carbon is already pyramidalized ~15 deg out of its C/O/H plane. For a formally non-bonded neutral aldehyde + weakly basic (amide-like) imine this is a heavily strained, charge-separated arrangement (vdW C...N ~3.3 A), so these four are placed last. This is the largest uncertainty in the ranking: if the reference method spuriously stabilizes such n->pi* adducts they could be lower than estimated. Three further conformers have a mild version of this contact (18: 2.84, 2: 2.92, 6: 3.03 A) and are penalized only slightly.

3) tau2 (CH2–O): d(C5...C13) = 3.62-3.64 A (anti, the ester-alkyl minimum) in 8, 11, 1, 3, 16, 15, 13, 25; ~3.2-3.36 A (skew, ~105 deg) in 26, 18, 10, 24, 14, 6, 7, 9, 19, 2, 27; ~2.84-3.13 A (gauche, ~85-90 deg) in 22, 21, 28, 17, 23, 5, 4 and in the strained set. Anti is taken as best, the gauche/skew forms ~0.4-0.5 kcal higher.

4) tau1: gauche (d(C6...O12) = 2.84-3.00 A) places the ether oxygen 38 deg off the carbonyl normal, i.e. a favourable O(ether)->C=O n->pi* contact (8, 11: 2.84; 1, 3: 2.92; also 10, 14, 9, 24, 28, 21, 26, 19, 13, 15, 16); anti (3.6-3.8 A: 25, 22, 5, 4, 7, 23, 27) is neutral; the intermediate ~3.15 A values (12, 20, 29, 30, 17) are on the eclipsing shoulder and are penalized.

5) Aldehyde rotamer: O7 eclipsing the methyl (d(O7...C1) ~2.80: 8, 11, 1, 3, 10, 14, 24, 9, 2, 6, 18, 22, 28) is taken as best by analogy with propanal (alkyl-syn favoured ~0.9 kcal); O7 eclipsing the bulkier CH2O group (d(O7...C9) ~2.80: 25, 5, 4, 27, 17) slightly worse; O7 eclipsing the methine H (d(O7...H17) ~2.55: 16, 15, 13, 21, 26, 19, 23, 7) worst.

6) Extra contact penalties: 17 additionally has an in-plane O7...O12 contact of 3.16 A (lone-pair/dipole repulsion) on top of a skewed tau1, making it the worst of the 'normal' conformers.

Summing these terms: 8, 11, 1, 3 (anti tau2 + gauche tau1 with O...C=O n->pi* + methyl-syn CHO, no close contacts) are best and essentially degenerate; 25 (fully extended anti/anti) and 28 follow; then the anti-tau2/H-eclipsed set (16, 15, 13) and the skew-tau2/methyl-syn set (10, 14, 24, 9); then 22 and the conformers combining two mild penalties (5, 4, 2, 6, 18); then those with H-eclipsed aldehyde plus skew/gauche tau2 (21, 27, 26, 19, 23, 7); then 17; finally the four strained N...C=O structures (30, 12, 29, 20, ordered by increasing shortness of that contact). Differences within tiers are only a few tenths of a kcal/mol and the ordering there is uncertain.

STRUCTURE. All 30 files are the same C8H14O: a cyclohexene ring C5-C6=C7-C8-C9-C10 (C6=C7 is the short 1.32 Å bond) carrying a CH3 on the allylic carbon C5 and a CH2OH (C13-O14-H15) on C9, i.e. (5-methylcyclohex-3-en-1-yl)methanol. The two substituents are 1,3 on the ring and, by projecting the C5-CH3 and C9-CH2OH bonds onto the ring normal in every file, they are always on the SAME face (cis-1,3). Hence the ring can put both groups pseudo-equatorial (best) or both axial (1,3-diaxial clash), or escape into a boat/twist form.

RING-FORM DIAGNOSTIC. For each conformer I built the plane of the four (nearly coplanar, checked to <0.1 Å) atoms C5-C6=C7-C8 and measured the signed out-of-plane heights h(C9), h(C10), plus the torsion about C9-C10 and the C(methyl)...C(CH2OH) distance:
  (i) HALF-CHAIR, DIEQUATORIAL: h(C9)/h(C10) of opposite sign, |h| ~0.33-0.45; torsion C8-C9-C10-C5 ~65 deg (fully staggered); CH2OH bond nearly in-plane (cos to normal ~0.15); Me...CH2OH >4.5 Å. Conformers 3, 8, 15, 16, 19, 21, 24, 25, 29.
  (ii) DIAXIAL (flattened half-chair): h ~ (+0.5 to +0.63, ~-0.1); CH2OH exactly perpendicular to the ring (cos ~0.99, axial) and the allylic methyl pseudo-axial; the tell-tale 1,3-diaxial contact C1...C13 = 3.38-3.51 Å, and the ring is visibly flattened on the C10-C5 side to relieve it. Conformers 5, 6, 9, 12, 13, 22, 26, 27. Cost ~3.5-4.5 kcal/mol (axial CH2OH ~1.8 + pseudo-axial allylic Me ~1 + mutual syn-axial repulsion).
  (iii) BOAT/TWIST-BOAT: h(C9) and h(C10) of the SAME sign (~+1.05 to +1.14, or ~-0.9), torsion about C9-C10 only 5-10 deg (two eclipsed ring bonds), and the CH2OH sits in the flagpole position (cos to normal ~0.9) close (2.4-2.5 Å) to the flagpole H on C10. Conformers 2, 4, 7, 11, 14, 17, 18, 20, 23, 28, 30 plus the more twisted 1 (0.89/0.55) and the shallower boats 10, 14 (~0.9, CH2OH pseudo-equatorial). Cost ~3-4.5 kcal/mol; these relieve the diaxial clash (Me...CH2OH 4.7-4.9 Å) but pay ring torsional/flagpole strain.

HYDROGEN BONDING. There is only one heteroatom, so the only intramolecular H-bond available is O-H...pi to the C6=C7 double bond, and it requires the CH2OH to lie over the ring (axial or flagpole). Measuring H15 to the alkene carbons and the O-H...C angle:
  20: H15...C7 = 2.33 Å, O-H...C 162 deg -> a genuine, almost linear O-H...pi bond (worth ~1.5-2 kcal), partially paying for its boat ring.
  27: 2.33 Å, 130 deg; 22: 2.39/2.40 Å over the bond midpoint, 131 deg; 1: 2.49 Å, 117 deg -> moderate/weak bonds that partly offset the diaxial (27, 22) or twist (1) penalty.
  2 and 18: H15...C7 2.61 Å but O-H...C only ~101 deg (O, not H, points at the pi cloud; O...C7 ~2.95 Å) -> essentially no stabilization, if anything a mildly repulsive lone-pair/pi contact.
  All other conformers have the OH pointing into free space (no H-bond).

FINE STRUCTURE INSIDE THE BEST GROUP. Among the nine diequatorial half-chairs the differences are small (<1 kcal). I used (a) the CH2OH rotamer: O14 anti to a ring carbon (one gauche interaction: 15, 24, 29, 25, 3, 21) is taken as slightly better than O anti to the C9-H (gauche to both ring carbons: 8, 19, 16); (b) symmetry/regularity of the half-chair pucker (15: 0.385/0.397 and 29, 24 are the most regular; 16 is the most flattened, 0.33/0.45); (c) minor contacts: 21 has an H15...H(C10) contact of 2.14 Å, 16 has H15...C10 2.66 Å. This ordering is the most uncertain part of the ranking.

Among the eight diaxial conformers, geometries are nearly identical (C1...C13 3.38-3.51 Å, OH pointing away), so I ordered by the residual diaxial distance and by the presence of the O-H...pi bond (27, 22 clearly better). Among the plain boats I put the shallower, pseudo-equatorial ones (10, 14) first, then those free of extra contacts (11, 17), and last those with additional close contacts (23: H15...H(C8) 2.06 Å; 7: 2.08 Å; 28: H15...H(C10) 2.21 Å) or unfavourable O/pi contacts (2, 18).

OVERALL: diequatorial half-chairs (no axial strain, staggered ring, no clashes) < boat/diaxial forms that recover ~1-2 kcal through an O-H...pi bond < diaxial half-chairs without H-bond < plain flagpole boats. The main uncertainties are (1) the exact ordering inside the diequatorial family, and (2) whether the 1,3-diaxial half-chairs really lie below the flagpole boats - their computed strain estimates (~4 kcal each) are within the error of this analysis.

All 30 structures are the same molecule, HOCH2-CH(CH3)-CH2-CH2-NH-CHO (N-(4-hydroxy-3-methylbutyl)formamide). The dominant energetic discriminator for such a flexible bifunctional chain is the intramolecular hydrogen bond, because the covalent framework is strain-free (no rings) and only torsional/steric terms remain. Two H-bond motifs are geometrically possible: (a) the hydroxyl donating to the amide carbonyl oxygen (O19-H20...O10), which closes a large but easily formed pseudo-ring and combines the best donor (alcohol OH) with the best acceptor (amide C=O); (b) the amide N-H donating to the hydroxyl oxygen (N8-H12...O19), a smaller 7-membered pseudo-ring but a weaker donor/acceptor pair. I measured H...O distances and O-H...O / N-H...O angles for every conformer.

Motif (a), OH...O=C (strongest set): 7 (1.87 A, 162 deg), 21 (1.91, 170), 30 (1.92, 171), 8 (1.92, 166), 23 (1.91, 157), 9 (1.98, 176), 4 (2.00, 168), 14 (1.94, 155), 1 (2.09, 147), 5 (2.11, 147). Ranking within this family follows a distance/linearity figure of merit: 7, 21, 30, 8 are essentially degenerate (short and nearly linear); 9 is perfectly linear but slightly longer; 23 and 4 are good; 14 is somewhat bent; 1 and 5 are both long (~2.1 A) and bent (~147 deg), so their H-bond is clearly weaker.

Motif (b), NH...OH: 10 (1.91, 147), 6 (1.92, 144), 24 (1.93, 143), 25 (2.02, 146), 15 (2.03, 146), and two poor, strongly bent cases 19 (2.18, 130) and 18 (2.17, 128). Even the best of these should lie above the non-bonded conformers but below the OH...O=C family, since N-H is a poorer donor and an sp3 alcohol O a poorer acceptor; the 143-147 deg angles further reduce the gain. 18 and 19 are so bent/long that their stabilization (~1 kcal) is roughly cancelled by the gauche coiling needed to form them, so they sit at the boundary with the non-H-bonded set.

No-H-bond set: 11, 13, 27, 28, 17, 22, 29, 16, 3, 2, 20, 26, 12. Here I used backbone extension as the proxy for torsional strain (O19...O10 separation, i.e. how many gauche C-C/C-N torsions are present without any H-bond payoff): 11 (6.03 A), 13 (5.81), 27 (5.79), 28 (5.77), 17 (5.75), 29 (5.61), 16 (5.34), 3 (5.28), 22 (4.72), 2 (4.70), 20 (4.59), 26 (4.50), 12 (3.95). The extended, nearly all-anti chains (11, 13, 27, 28, 17) pay no gauche penalty and keep the two dipoles apart; 22 (H12...O19 2.45 A but only 116 deg) and 2 (2.71 A, 71 deg off-axis) retain only vestigial polar contacts, so they gain little for their coiling. The worst cases are the compact conformers whose polar groups approach each other without any productive H-bond geometry: 20 and 26 (coiled, OH pointing away from both acceptors) and especially 12, where the two oxygens are only 3.95 A apart with the OH rotated away (O-H...O ~86 deg off-axis) and the N-H also misdirected (2.66 A, 86 deg) - a compact, dipole-repulsive arrangement with gauche strain and no compensating H-bond.

Uncertainties: (i) the top four OH...O=C conformers (7, 21, 30, 8) differ by only 0.05 A and a few degrees, so their internal order is essentially arbitrary; (ii) the relative weight of a bent NH...OH bond versus 2-3 gauche torsions is the main systematic uncertainty, i.e. 18/19 could easily fall below the extended non-bonded structures 11/13; (iii) within the non-bonded block the ordering rests on extendedness alone and individual methyl/CH2 rotamer details (no severe H...H contacts below ~2.0 A were found in any structure) could shuffle neighbours by a few tenths of a kcal.

Connectivity (identical in all files): CH3–CH(CH2OH)–CH(OH)–CH(aziridin-2-yl), i.e. a 1,3-diol-type arrangement (primary O7–H8 on C6, secondary O20–H21 on C12) plus an aziridine N15–H16 that is 1,2 to the secondary OH (O20–C12–C13–N15). Ring strain is identical everywhere (aziridine), so relative energies are governed by (i) the intramolecular O–H...O hydrogen bond closing the 6-membered ring H–O7–C6–C5–C12–O20, (ii) a weak 5-ring N–H...O20 contact, (iii) an occasional 7-ring O7–H...N15 bond, and (iv) the gauche/anti pattern of the bulky substituents across the C5–C12 bond.

- Strong 6-ring O–H...O: 12 (1.93 A, 143 deg), 13 (1.95, 142), 6 (1.96, 141), 1 (1.96, 140), 21 (1.96, 140), 10 (1.96, 140), 16 (1.98, 140), 20 (1.98, 138), 7 (2.01, 138), 11 (2.01, 137), 24 (2.02, 132), 14 (2.03, 135), 30 (2.04, 134), 9 (2.04, 135), 22 (2.04, 133), 29 (2.06, 131), 4 (2.07, 132), 27 (2.08, 128).

Family I therefore gets a small bonus; within Family II, 11 (C1...C13 = 2.94 A) and 9 (C6...C13 = 2.94 A) are the most compressed.

Ranking logic: primary weight to H-bond length/linearity, secondary bonus for the extra N–H...O20 contact, small bonus for the anti (Family I) skeleton, penalty for compressed gauche contacts, and the non-bonded conformers last (extended strain-free ones above the strained gauche ones). Uncertainties: (a) the true weight of the 7-ring O–H...N in 18 relative to the 6-ring O–H...O set (it could easily move up several places); (b) the ~0.2-0.4 kcal spread inside the block 6/21/10/7/22/14/24/11/9/29 is within the noise of this geometric estimate; (c) the internal order of the six extended non-H-bonded conformers (3, 26, 28, 25, 19, 17) is essentially arbitrary since they differ only in remote torsions.

All 30 structures are the same molecule: an acetimidate ester, CH3-C(=NH)-O-CH2CH2CH2CH2-OH (atoms: C1 methyl, C2 imidate carbon, N3/H4 imine NH, O5 ester oxygen, C6-C7-C8-C9 the butylene chain, O10/H11 the terminal hydroxyl). Checking the C6-O5-C2=N3 dihedral in several conformers (20, 3, 22) gives ~0-5 deg in all cases, so the imidate unit (O-alkyl syn to N-H) is identical everywhere; the energy differences therefore come from (i) intramolecular hydrogen bonding of the terminal OH and (ii) gauche/eclipsing strain along the O-CH2CH2CH2CH2-OH chain.

Hydrogen bonding: I measured H11...O5, H11...N3 and H4(NH)...O10 distances. No conformer places the hydroxyl H near the imine nitrogen, so the only H-bonds found are OH...O(ester) closing a seven-membered ring: conformer 3 (H...O = 1.87 A, O-H...O angle 159 deg), 18 (1.90 A, 154 deg), 20 (1.90 A, 153 deg), 2 (2.02 A, 154 deg), 12 (2.09 A, 139 deg) and 13 (2.22 A, 138 deg, weak/bent). Conformer 14 has only a weak, strongly bent N-H...O(H) contact (H4...O10 = 2.45 A, angle ~130 deg); conformer 21 has a non-bonding H11...O5 = 2.78 A at 118 deg, i.e. essentially no H-bond. All remaining conformers have the OH pointing into space (O...O and O...N separations > 4 A).

Torsional strain: using 1,4-distance proxies (anti ~3.7-3.9 A, gauche ~2.9-3.2 A) for C2-O5-C6-C7 (T1), O5-C6-C7-C8 (T2), C6-C7-C8-C9 (T3) and C7-C8-C9-O10 (T4): 23 is the most extended non-bonded chain (T2, T3, T4 all anti, only T1 gauche); 9, 28, 29 have the favourable anti C-O-C-C torsion plus two anti/two gauche; 8, 10, 16, 17 have two anti C-C torsions but a gauche T1; 11, 15, 24, 25 have one anti C-C torsion; 1, 6, 21, 26, 22, 30, 7, 27, 19, 4, 5 are progressively more coiled (three to four gauche/skew torsions) without any compensating H-bond, which makes them the poorest.

Weighing an intramolecular OH...O bond (roughly 2.5-4 kcal/mol depending on length and linearity) against ~0.5-0.9 kcal/mol per gauche interaction: the H-bonded set (3, 18, 20, 12, 2) is clearly best. 3 combines the shortest, most linear H-bond with an anti O-alkyl torsion, so it is placed first; 18 is very similar (H-bond 1.90 A, near-anti T1). 20 has the same H-bond length but a fully coiled, all-gauche backbone, and 12 trades a slightly longer/more bent H-bond for an anti T1 - these two are essentially degenerate and their order is uncertain. 2 and then the weakly bonded 13 follow. Among non-bonded structures the extended 23 is best, followed by the T1-anti forms 28, 29 and 9, then the two-anti forms 8, 10, 16, 17, and finally the tightly coiled 26, 21, 1 and 6, which pay three-to-four gauche penalties (and in 21 an unproductive O-H orientation) with no H-bond compensation.

Uncertainties: differences within the non-H-bonded block are only a few tenths of a kcal/mol and my anti/gauche assignment via 1,4-distances cannot distinguish ~80-110 deg skew torsions cleanly (conformers 3, 18, 20, 14, 22 contain such distorted torsions); the relative order of 20 vs 12 vs 2 and the whole middle block should be regarded as tentative.

All 30 files are the same molecule, 2-(2-cyclopropylethoxy)acetonitrile: N≡C–CH2–O–CH2–CH2–(cyclopropyl). Bond-distance checks confirm an intact cyclopropane (three ~1.50 Å C–C bonds) attached to the chain terminus, so ring strain is identical in every structure and there are no H-bond donors. Relative energies therefore come almost entirely from the four rotatable torsions plus any distorted (near-barrier) dihedrals or close contacts. Numbering atoms as listed: N1, C2(nitrile C), C3(OCH2CN), O4, C5(OCH2), C6(CH2), C7(ring CH), C8/C9(ring CH2).

Relevant torsions and how I measured them (1,4-distance proxy, calibrated: anti ≈ 3.6–3.8 Å, gauche ≈ 2.9–3.1 Å, ~90° ≈ 3.25–3.4 Å; several were verified by explicit dihedral calculation):
 T2 = C2–C3–O4–C5 (rotation about the O–CH2CN bond)
 T3 = C3–O4–C5–C6 (the ether C–O–C–C torsion)
 T4 = O4–C5–C6–C7
 T5 = chain orientation on the cyclopropyl CH (all conformers turned out to have essentially the same ~2.8 Å C5···H(C7) value, i.e. the same ring orientation, so T5 does not discriminate).

Results: (a=anti, g=gauche, m≈90°)
 2 (a,a,a), 27 (a,a,a), 23 (a,a,g), 30 (g,a,a), 17 (g,a,a), 28/19/26/5/16 (g,a,g), 29/12/9 (a,g,a), 4 (a,g,g), 6/15/24/10/25 (g,g,a), 1/7/14/18/11/22/3 (g,g,g), 8 (g, T3≈100°, g), 13 (g,g,T4≈88°), 21 (g,g,T4≈95°), 20 (g,g,T4≈98°, verified by vector algebra).

Energetic weighting: (i) T3 is the classic dialkyl-ether C–O–C–C torsion, where anti is strongly preferred (~1–1.5 kcal/mol over gauche); this is the dominant term. (ii) T4 (O–C–C–C) anti is preferred by a few tenths of a kcal/mol. (iii) T2 is nearly degenerate: gauche loses little sterically because the nitrile is linear and slim, and it gains a weak anomeric nO→σ*(C–CN) stabilization, so anti and gauche ROCH2CN forms are essentially isoenergetic — this is the main source of uncertainty, so all-anti (2, 27) and g,a,a (30, 17) forms are interleaved at the top. (iv) Any dihedral pinned near 90–100° sits close to a rotational barrier and is penalized (~1 kcal/mol): this puts 20, 21, 13 (distorted O–C–C–C) and 8 (distorted C–O–C–C) at the bottom. (v) No conformer shows a genuinely short stabilizing or repulsive contact: the nitrile N is >2.7 Å from all H atoms; the shortest C–H···N contacts (7: 2.75 Å; 14: 2.85 Å) are only weakly attractive and cannot compensate for their all-gauche backbones. Within a torsion class I broke ties by how close each gauche dihedral is to the ideal 60° (smaller 1,4 distance = less strain toward the 120° barrier).

So the ordering is: extended chains with anti ether torsion first (2, 30, 27, 17), then anti-ether/gauche-terminal (5, 16, 28, 19, 26, 23), then gauche-ether species (15, 10, 29, 6, 12, 24, 9, 25), then all-gauche coils (18, 3, 4, 1, 11, 14, 22, 7), and finally the geometrically strained near-eclipsed ones (8, 13, 21, 20). Differences inside each block are only a few tenths of a kcal/mol and their internal order is low-confidence; the block boundaries (anti vs gauche C–O–C–C, and normal vs ~90° torsions) are the robust part of the ranking.

STRUCTURE: All 30 files are the same C7H12O2 skeleton: a seven-membered cyclic ether (oxepane-type ring: O11-C12H2-C4=C5H-C6H2-C8H2-C10H2-O11) carrying an exocyclic CH2OH (C3-O1-H2) on the sp2 carbon C4. Two degrees of unsaturation = one ring + one endocyclic C=C. Therefore the energy differences must come from (i) the pucker of the 7-membered ring (torsional/eclipsing strain, twist of the ring double bond), and (ii) the orientation of the CH2OH group (OH...O(ether) contact, or OH...pi contact with the C4=C5 bond).

RING PUCKER: I characterized the pucker with the ring 1,4-distances d(C5,C10), d(C6,O11), d(C8,C12), d(C4,C10) (these map monotonically onto the corresponding torsions) plus d(C12,C6) for the twist of the C4=C5 bond. Four distinct families appear:
(IV) d ~ 3.19/3.12/3.06/3.14, C12-C4=C5-C6 ~ 0 deg: all sp3 torsions 68-85 deg, staggered throughout, planar (untwisted) alkene -> lowest-strain twist-chair. Members: 5, 16, 23, 24, 25, 27, 28, 29, 30.
(I) d ~ 2.89/3.29/2.81/2.87: torsions ~30/45/86/50/57, still all staggered but the ring alkene is twisted ~20-25 deg -> slightly strained. Members: 4, 6, 7, 15, 19.
(II) d ~ 3.22/2.80/2.90/3.18: contains one partly eclipsed C6-C8-C10-O11 torsion (~35 deg) plus a ~23 deg alkene twist -> ~1 kcal more strained. Members: 1, 3, 8, 9, 11, 13, 17, 21.
(III) d ~ 2.95/2.71/3.25/2.88: the C6-C8-C10-O11 torsion is only ~25 deg (clearly eclipsed CH2-CH2) -> most torsionally strained family. Members: 2, 10, 12, 14, 18, 20, 22, 26.

HYDROXYL INTERACTIONS: The hydroxyl H2...O11(ether) distance never reaches true H-bond range because the O1-C3-C4-C12-O11 path is constrained by the sp2 carbon; the best contacts are H2...O11 = 2.89 (7), 2.92 (23), 3.28 (28), 3.31 (6), 3.9-4.1 (8, 22, 13, 24, 14), everything else >4.3 (no interaction). A second, competing stabilization is an intramolecular OH...pi contact: H2 to the midpoint of C4=C5 is 2.61-2.65 A in conformers 10, 11, 15, 19, 21, 26, 27, 30 (genuine, if weak, OH...pi), ~2.9-3.0 A (marginal) in 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 17, 18, 20, 23, 28, and 3.2-3.7 A (OH pointing away from both acceptors, no stabilization) in 1, 2, 3, 9, 12, 13, 14, 16, 22, 24, 25, 29.

No conformer shows a hard steric problem (no H...H below ~2.0 A, no transannular contact under ~2.2 A), so the ranking is set by: family IV < I < II < III for ring strain (steps of ~0.4-0.5 kcal), with a -0.4 to -0.8 kcal credit for a short OH...O(ether) contact and about -0.7 kcal for an OH...pi contact.

RESULT: the twist-chair family IV members that also orient the OH toward the ether oxygen (23) or over the alkene (27, 30, 28) are best; the alkene-twisted family I follows, with 7 (best OH...O of the whole set, 2.89 A) and the OH...pi members 19/15 near the top of that group; family II conformers with an eclipsing penalty come next, and the eclipsed family III (2, 12, 14, 22, 18, 20) is last, only partly rescued when an OH...pi contact is present (10, 26).

UNCERTAINTY: the ring-family gaps and the relative weight of a long OH...O(ether) contact versus a weak OH...pi contact are both small (a few tenths of a kcal), so neighbouring entries (especially within a family, e.g. 27/30/28, 19/15, 29/25/16, 9/3/1, 12/2) are essentially interchangeable; the clearest statements are that eclipsed family III conformers with no OH stabilization (2, 12, 14) are the least stable and that 23/27/30/7 are among the most stable.

All 30 files describe the same rigid bicycle: a fused oxetane/cyclobutane core (2-oxabicyclo[2.2.0]hexane; bridgeheads = atoms 7 and 13, ether O = atom 12) carrying a 2-hydroxyethyl chain on ring carbon atom 5. Checking the ring geometry (plane normal of the C5/C7/C13/C15 cyclobutane vs. the position of the oxetane CH2) shows the chain sits on the same (concave/endo) face in every structure, so the core is essentially invariant and all energy differences come from (i) an intramolecular O-H...O(ether) hydrogen bond, (ii) the rotamer about the C5-C4 (ring-CH2) bond, and (iii) the O-C-C-C torsion of the chain.

(1) H-bonds: computing H(2)...O(12) for all 30, only two conformers have a real contact: 30 (H...O = 2.00 A, O-H...O = 163 deg, O...O 2.94) and 15 (H...O = 2.06 A, angle 153 deg, O...O 2.95). Both close an 8-membered O-H...O-C-C-C-C-O loop. All others have H...O(ether) > 4 A, i.e. a free OH.

(2) Rotamer about the exocyclic C-C bond: torsions/1,4-distances of C1(atom3) to the three substituents on the ring carbon (bridgehead C7, CH2 C15, H6) sort the structures into three staggered families (C1 anti to C15 'anti-F', anti to C7 'anti-E', anti to H 'anti-H6') and one clearly eclipsed family (C1 syn-periplanar to the C5-C15 ring bond, torsion ~0-10 deg, C1...C15 ~3.0 A with accompanying H...H contacts of 2.3 A). Eclipsed (syn) members: 4, 5, 15, 16, 22, 25, 26, 28 - these carry ~1-1.5 kcal of torsional strain. 'anti-H6' places C1 between the two ring bonds and brings it to ~2.6 A of an oxetane CH2 hydrogen (e.g. 29), so it is slightly worse than anti-F/anti-E, which point the chain cleanly away from the bicycle.

(3) O-C-C-C torsion (calibrated from O(1)...C(5) distances and check dihedrals): anti (~160-180 deg) in 5, 10, 12, 14, 20, 24, 26, 28, 29; normal gauche (52-70 deg) in 1, 3, 6, 7, 9, 11, 13, 19, 21, 23, 27, 30; distorted, partly eclipsing values (72-90 deg) in 4, 8, 15, 16, 17, 18, 22, 25; and a badly eclipsing 111 deg in 2 (verified by explicit dihedral).

Putting these together: 30 is best (H-bond plus fully staggered chain); 15 keeps the H-bond but pays the eclipsed ring-bond torsion, so it is second. Next come the strain-free, fully extended conformers with anti O-C-C-C and staggered ring rotamer (12, 10, 14 anti-F; 24, 20 anti-E) - these are essentially degenerate, differing only in the hydroxyl rotamer (anti in 12, gauche in 10/14). Then the same staggered rotamers with a gauche chain torsion (9, 27, 13, 19, 21 anti-F; 7, 1, 3, 6, 11, 23 anti-E), with 29 (anti-H6 but anti chain) interleaved. 8 is demoted slightly within this group because its curled OH points its hydrogen at the bridgehead carbon (H...C 2.5 A, O...C 3.2 A) with no acceptor. 18 and 17 combine the more crowded anti-H6 rotamer with distorted 72-85 deg chain torsions. The eclipsed family follows: 28, 26, 5 keep an anti chain torsion (only one bad torsion), 2 has the worst O-C-C-C value (111 deg), and 16, 4, 25, 22 stack the eclipsed ring torsion on top of distorted 72-88 deg chain torsions with 2.2-2.4 A H...H contacts, making them least stable.

Uncertainty: the two H-bonded structures are confidently lowest, and the eclipsed/distorted set (16, 4, 25, 22, 2) confidently highest in energy; the middle ~18 conformers differ by only a few tenths of a kcal/mol (rotamer type, gauche vs anti chain, OH rotamer), so their relative order is soft and could easily reshuffle at a higher level of theory.

Connectivity analysis (bond distances ~1.53-1.55 Å) shows all 30 structures are cis-3-(2-hydroxyethyl)cyclobutan-1-ol: a cyclobutane ring C5-C7-C10-C13, with an OH on C10 and a -CH2CH2OH chain on C5, the two substituents on the same ring face (checked by projecting C4-C5 and O11-C10 vectors on the ring normal: both positive). Ring strain, bond lengths and angles are essentially identical in all conformers, so the ranking is governed by (i) intramolecular O-H...O hydrogen bonding across the ring face, (ii) the two chain torsions O1-C3-C4-C5 (tau1) and C3-C4-C5-X (tau2), and (iii) O/O lone-pair repulsion when the two hydroxyls are close but misaligned.

H-bond survey (O1...O11 distance, then H...O and O-H...O angle): 25: 2.87 / 1.91 Å / ~170 deg; 19: 2.88 / 1.92 Å / ~172 deg; 30: 2.89 / 1.94 Å / ~167 deg; 11: 2.92 / 1.99 Å / ~160 deg. These four are the only genuine hydrogen-bonded conformers and must be clearly lowest; in 25 and 19 the primary OH donates to the ring OH, in 30 and 11 the ring OH donates to the chain OH. Ranking inside this group follows H...O length and linearity (25 ~ 19 > 30 > 11); the differences are small (a few tenths of a kcal) and this internal order is the least certain part.

All four H-bonded structures achieve the contact with a favourable chain rotamer: tau2 places C3 anti to the ring C-H (C3...C7 and C3...C13 both ~3.1-3.3 Å, i.e. chain pointing outward, no over-ring clash) and only tau1 is gauche (O1...C5 ~3.1 Å), a cheap price for a ~3-4 kcal H-bond.

For the other 26 conformers no O-H...O contact exists (O1...O11 = 3.8-6.6 Å). They were ordered using 1-4 distances as torsion proxies (O1...C5 ~3.75-3.85 Å = anti tau1, ~2.95-3.10 Å = gauche; C3...C(ring) ~3.94 Å = chain anti to a ring carbon, both ~3.0-3.3 Å = chain outward, anti to the ring H):
- 20 is the best non-bonded conformer: tau1 anti (3.82 Å) AND chain outward (3.16/3.22 Å), fully staggered, no contact below van der Waals limits.
- 23 (O...O 4.05 Å, H12...O1 3.30 Å but 44 deg off linear) and 15 (O...O 3.85 Å, both O-H pointing away) are 'almost' H-bonded: 23 keeps a weak electrostatic attraction (outward chain, gauche tau1) and ranks just below 20; 15 has the two oxygens close with lone pairs facing each other, which is at best neutral, so it sits in the middle.
- Conformers with anti tau1 and the chain anti to a ring carbon (14, 21, 9, 10, 22, 18) follow: extended, staggered, only the mild over-ring rotamer penalty.
- Conformers with gauche tau1 and the chain anti to a ring carbon (13, 12, 3, 24, 26, 29, 2, 4, 28, 16, 6, 17, 1, 27, 7) pay both a gauche penalty and the over-ring rotamer; within this large, nearly isoenergetic block I put those with intermediate O...O separation (5.2-5.6 Å, partial dipole cancellation) slightly below the fully splayed ones (6.2-6.3 Å, maximal molecular dipole).
